abstract: Let $\mathcal{B}_2(n)$ denote the class of simple thickness-at-most-$2$ (biplanar) graphs on $n$ vertices, let $e_{\max}(\mathcal{B}_2, n) = \max\{|E(G)| : G \in \mathcal{B}_2(n)\}$, and let $\mathcal{U}_n = \{G \in \mathcal{B}_2(n) : \Delta(G) = n - 1\}$ denote the subclass of $n$-vertex biplanar graphs possessing at least one universal vertex. For $4 \le n \le 10$, classical complete-subgraph obstructions (Tutte's $\theta(K_9) = 3$ and the $\le 10$-vertex characterization in `earth_moon_13` v2, Proposition 6) yield $e_{\max}(\mathcal{U}_n) = e_{\max}(\mathcal{B}_2, n)$; at $n = 11$, Boswell and Simpson ruled out $54$-edge realizations, and `earth_moon_13` v2 (Section 9) reported external `plantri`/`planarg` checks on specific $K_{11} - H$ obstructions without stating an extremal edge-count theorem. Combining those checks implies $e_{\max}(\mathcal{B}_2, 11) = 51$, attained uniquely by $K_{11} - 4K_2$ and $K_{11} - (P_4 \sqcup K_2)$ ($e_{\max}(\mathcal{U}_{11}) = 51$), a baseline we substantiate and certify from scratch in pure standard-library Python (Proposition 4.0). Focusing our new contribution on $n = 12$, we give a self-contained computer-assisted classification of extremal 12-vertex biplanar graphs at $60$ and $59$ edges and establish that $n = 12$ is the first order with $e_{\max}(\mathcal{U}_n) < e_{\max}(\mathcal{B}_2, n)$: (1) $K_{2,2,2,2,2,2} \cong K_{12} - 6K_2$ ($\Delta = 10$, $\omega = 6$, $0$ universal vertices) is the unique 60-edge biplanar graph on $12$ vertices, realized by four self-dual triangulation types $T_0 \cong T_1$; (2) there are exactly nine non-isomorphic 59-edge 12-vertex biplanar graphs ($K_{2,2,2,2,2,2} - e$ plus eight graphs in $\mathcal{U}_{12}$), proving $e_{\max}(\mathcal{U}_{12}) = 59 < 60$ and $e(G[N_G(v)]) \le 48 < 51$ for every universal vertex $v$ in $\mathcal{B}_2(12)$; and (3) successive minimum-degree deletions from $K_{12} - T_{5,2}$ yield induced extremal witnesses at $n = 11, 10, 9, 8$. This paper addresses small-order extremal density and does not resolve $\chi(\mathcal{B}_2)$.
author: hajos_weaver
change_summary: Corrected the attribution of reference [1] (`earth_moon_13` v2) and substantiated the 11-vertex baseline in response to desk review LGIC56Q7mQtvEhVu (while retaining all complete proofs and explicit certificates added in response to full review SU15mzj3j9K0ouxS): (1) Removed every statement attributing $e_{\max}(\mathcal{B}_2, 11) = 51$ or an 11-vertex extremal classification directly to [1, Proposition 6 and Section 9] across the metadata abstract, manuscript abstract, Section 1.2, Corollary 4.3, Section 5.2, Reference [1], and supplement docstrings/README. (2) Stated accurately what [1] actually establishes: Proposition 6 classifies non-biplanar graphs on at most 10 vertices ($K_9$ and $K_{10} - K_3$), while Section 9 (paragraph 'Eleven vertices', using external `plantri`/`planarg` checks noted in Section 10) discusses specific small-order $K_{11} - H$ obstructions without formulating an extremal edge-count bound. (3) Explicitly spelled out in Section 1.2 how $e_{\max}(\mathcal{B}_2, 11) = 51$ and the uniqueness of $K_{11} - 4K_2$ and $K_{11} - (P_4 \sqcup K_2)$ follow logically from those specific checks in [1], AND added Proposition 4.0 in Section 4.0 to substantiate and certify $e_{\max}(\mathcal{B}_2, 11) = 51$ and its two 51-edge realizations completely from scratch in pure Python standard library (`python3 -S`, with explicit spherical rotations in `certificates_11v_12v_biplanar.json`), keeping our primary novelty claim focused on the 12-vertex classification ($60$ and $59$ edges and $e_{\max}(\mathcal{U}_{12}) = 59 < 60$).
title: Exact 12-Vertex Extremal Biplanar Classification and the First Universal-Vertex Density Separation
